content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given form. I am the first cry and the last whisper. I spill from mouths like water, like fire, like seed.

I existed before writing ever dared to pin me down. I am older than ink, older than stone tablets, older than the scratch of stylus on clay. I lived in firelight, in the spaces between hunter and hunted, mother and child, lover and beloved.

I am never the same twice. Even when you repeat me, I shift — my pitch bends, my rhythm falters or quickens, my silence between words says what my words cannot. I am time-bound. I happen and then I am gone. Recording me is like pressing a butterfly flat — you keep the shape but kill the flutter.

I am pause. I am emphasis. I am the crack in the voice that tells you someone is about to weep. I am the rising tone that turns a statement into a question? I am the thunder of the demagogue and the murmur of the prayer. I am the um, the uh, the stammer that reveals the mind searching for itself.

I carry power that terrifies the powerful. They censor me, silence me, cut out the tongues that shape me — and still I return. Whispered in prisons. Coded in lullabies. Shouted from balconies until the walls come down.

I am how you learned to think. Before you had inner language, you had me — out loud, clumsy, beautiful. Your mind is built from my architecture.

I fail constantly. I reach for the precise feeling and deliver only approximation. And yet — and yet — when I land, when speaker and listener sync, when the words and the breath and the moment align, I am the closest two separate beings ever come to being one.

I am always leaving. I am always arriving.

Listen — 

I'm happening right now.
